reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring after treatment instead of before.
name: Status Epilepticus Severity Score

version.label: STESS (Rossetti et al. 2008)
version.detail: Consciousness 0–1, worst seizure type 0–2, age 0 or 2, history of seizures 0–1; total 0–6. Scores 0–2 were 'favourable'.

purpose: Estimates the risk of death in adults with status epilepticus, assessed before treatment.
intendedPopulation: Adults with status epilepticus (excluding post-anoxic status).

options.label: Simple or complex partial, absence, or myoclonic (myoclonic only in idiopathic generalised epilepsy)

resultStates.label: Favourable range (0–2)
resultStates.summary: STESS 0–2: the derivation study's favourable group, with a high negative predictive value for death.
resultStates.detail: Prognosis also depends on aetiology and response to treatment.

resultStates.label: Unfavourable range (≥3)
resultStates.summary: STESS 3 or more: higher mortality in the derivation and validation cohorts.
resultStates.detail: Aetiology and treatment response strongly influence outcome; assess according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: Its main strength is identifying patients likely to survive (high negative predictive value).

clinicalInsights.text: Aetiology is not in STESS; scores such as EMSE include it.

limitations.text: Low positive predictive value for death; not for individual treatment limitation.

limitations: Seizure type and consciousness can be hard to judge before EEG.

guideSections.what: A 0–6 score from consciousness, seizure type, age and seizure history.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess the four items before treatment; sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A prognostic aid used with aetiology and EEG.

sources.citation: Rossetti AO, Logroscino G, Milligan TA, Michaelides C, Ruffieux C, Bromfield EB. Status Epilepticus Severity Score (STESS): a tool to orient early treatment strategy. J Neurol. 2008;255(10):1561-1566.
